patient.chief_complaint: Progressive cognitive and gait decline at 58, with lifelong migraine with aura and a family history of early dementia and stroke
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Federica Nanni is a 58-year-old librarian on long-term sick leave who attends with her husband. She has had migraine with aura since her twenties, with prolonged sensory auras, and had two episodes of transient hemiparesis at 49 and 53 that were both attributed to complicated migraine without imaging. Over the past three years she has become progressively slower and less able to organise: she could not maintain the cataloguing system she had run for twenty years, has been on sick leave for eight months, and stopped driving four months ago after becoming disoriented on a route she had driven daily. Her husband describes apathy without sadness and is clear that this differs from her two previous depressive episodes, which responded to treatment. Walking changed two years ago, with small steps and urinary urgency. Her family history is striking: her mother developed a dementia with gait difficulty at 62 and died at 68 without a diagnosis, a maternal uncle had strokes from his late forties and died at 59, and her maternal grandmother was described as 'senile' from her sixties. Her blood pressure has been normal at every visit, she has never smoked and she has no diabetes. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation and no dream enactment.

findings.type: White matter hyperintensity of presumed vascular origin
findings.location: Confluent periventricular and deep white matter with symmetric involvement of both anterior temporal poles and both external capsules

signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: Extensive confluent hyperintensity; symmetric anterior temporal pole involvement and external capsule involvement, with subcortical U-fibre involvement

findings.location: Bilateral thalami, bilateral corona radiata, left putamen, pons

signal_characteristics.SWI: Deep distribution; no lobar microbleed and no cortical superficial siderosis

signal_characteristics.T2: Multiple perivascular spaces including the temporal lobes

findings.location: Mild global, medial temporal lobes preserved for age

volumetrics.anterior_temporal_pole_involvement: Present and symmetric — the most specific imaging marker of CADASIL
volumetrics.white_matter_lesion_volume: Estimated 58 mL, Fazekas 3, extreme for age

additional_observations: Symmetric anterior temporal pole white matter involvement is the most specific imaging marker of CADASIL and is present here; sporadic hypertensive small-vessel disease characteristically spares the anterior temporal poles
External capsule involvement and subcortical U-fibre involvement are further supportive markers
A 58 mL white matter lesion volume in a 58-year-old with normal blood pressure, normal lipids and no diabetes is far outside the sporadic range
Microbleeds are deep, which is expected in CADASIL and does not indicate amyloid angiopathy
mri.impression: Severe small-vessel arteriopathy with the specific imaging signature of CADASIL: symmetric anterior temporal pole and external capsule white matter involvement with confluent Fazekas 3 change, six lacunes and two deep microbleeds, in a 58-year-old without vascular risk factors. Medial temporal lobes are normal for age.

Reversible_cause_screen.clinical_significance: Normal — excludes hyperhomocysteinaemia as a cause of premature small-vessel disease

labs.interpretation: Every vascular risk marker is normal or favourable: HbA1c 5.2%, HDL 66 mg/dL, normal homocysteine, normal inflammatory markers and negative antiphospholipid antibodies. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative. The absence of any acquired cause is itself the finding in a 58-year-old with a severe small-vessel burden.

quantitative_data.pattern: subcortical executive with preserved recognition and naming

specialized_test.impression: A subcortical executive profile at the 3rd-8th percentile with intact recognition memory and naming, and informant-rated loss of instrumental function. The profile is that of a small-vessel arteriopathy, not of a cortical degeneration.

findings.performance: Digit span backwards 0/1, serial sevens 2/3 — impaired

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 21/30 in a university-educated librarian, with an executive and processing-speed profile, fully cue-responsive recall and apathy dissociated from depression. Instrumental and occupational function are lost. The profile is subcortical; the question is why a 58-year-old with no vascular risk factors has a subcortical vascular syndrome.

findings.value: Pathogenic (ACMG class 5): cysteine-altering variant in an EGF-like repeat, the established mechanism in CADASIL
Repeat 4 — the position associated with the more severe end of the phenotypic spectrum

output.impression: Pathogenic heterozygous cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variant in EGF-like repeat 4: CADASIL is confirmed. The variant position is associated with the more severe end of the spectrum, which fits the family history of stroke from the late forties. First-degree relatives should be offered genetic counselling.

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia due to CADASIL (cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy), NOTCH3 c.475C>T p.(Arg159Cys)

differential.key_features: The syndrome and the burden would fit, but she is 58 with normal blood pressure, normal lipids, no diabetes and no smoking history, and the anterior temporal pole involvement is a marker sporadic disease does not produce

This was the attribution for both episodes of transient hemiparesis and it delayed the diagnosis by nine years; migraine with aura is itself part of the CADASIL phenotype rather than an alternative to it

White matter lesions in a middle-aged woman, but the lesions are confluent and subcortical rather than periventricular ovoid and juxtacortical, there is no optic nerve or cord involvement, no gadolinium enhancement and no clinical relapse-remission pattern

differential.diagnosis: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
differential.key_features: Inflammatory markers are normal, there is no enhancement and no multifocal stenosis, and the family history points elsewhere
Two prior episodes responded to treatment; the current apathy is dissociated from mood on formal scales and accompanied by a gait disorder and pyramidal signs

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Progressive cognitive and gait decline from her mid-fifties with lifelong migraine with aura, two unimaged episodes of transient hemiparesis, and an autosomal-dominant pattern of early stroke and dementia across three generations, in the complete absence of vascular risk factors

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 21/30 with an executive and processing-speed profile, cue-responsive recall and apathy dissociated from depression, in a patient under 60 with no vascular risk factors

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Every acquired cause of premature small-vessel disease excluded — normal glycaemia, lipids, homocysteine, inflammatory markers and antiphospholipid antibodies — which makes a hereditary arteriopathy the leading explanation

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confluent Fazekas 3 white matter change with symmetric anterior temporal pole and external capsule involvement, six lacunes and two deep microbleeds in a 58-year-old — the imaging signature of CADASIL

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Subcortical executive profile with preserved recognition memory, and formal documentation of the occupational and instrumental loss

optimal_actions.action: Send NOTCH3 sequencing: onset before 60 with migraine with aura, a family history of stroke or early dementia and anterior temporal pole white matter involvement is the phenotype of hereditary small-vessel disease
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pathogenic NOTCH3 cysteine-altering variant confirming CADASIL, which establishes the diagnosis, explains three generations of the family history, and makes genetic counselling available to her son and her sister

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Confirm CADASIL genetically, offer genetic counselling to her son and her sister with a discussion of predictive testing, avoid triptans and stop the sumatriptan given the arteriopathy, treat migraine prophylactically without vasoconstrictors, control blood pressure conservatively without allowing hypotension in a patient with impaired autoregulation, avoid anticoagulation and smoking, refer for occupational assessment and disability support at 58, and arrange rehabilitation for the gait disorder
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Diagnosis established and cascaded to the family with counselling, vasoconstrictor migraine therapy stopped, blood pressure managed without hypotension, and occupational and disability support arranged for a patient of working age

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Recognise that a severe small-vessel burden in a patient under 60 without vascular risk factors requires a hereditary explanation
Look specifically for anterior temporal pole involvement, the most specific imaging marker of CADASIL
Exclude the acquired causes of premature small-vessel disease — homocysteine, inflammatory markers, antiphospholipid antibodies
Send NOTCH3 sequencing rather than settling for a descriptive diagnosis
Re-examine the previous attribution of transient hemiparesis to complicated migraine
Offer genetic counselling to first-degree relatives once the variant is confirmed
Stop triptans and avoid anticoagulation in a patient with this arteriopathy, and manage blood pressure without inducing hypotension
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue triptans in a patient with a confirmed cerebral arteriopathy
Do not anticoagulate: there is no embolic source and the arteriopathy carries a haemorrhagic risk
Do not lower blood pressure to hypotensive levels in a patient with impaired cerebral autoregulation
Do not test the teenage son without formal genetic counselling and consideration of the ethics of predictive testing in a minor
Do not accept 'complicated migraine' as the explanation for transient hemiparesis in a patient with this family history and imaging
key_reasoning_points: Age and the absence of risk factors are the entry point: a 58 mL white matter lesion volume in a normotensive non-diabetic non-smoker of 58 is outside the sporadic range and demands a hereditary explanation
Anterior temporal pole involvement is the imaging marker that distinguishes CADASIL from sporadic small-vessel disease, which characteristically spares those regions
Migraine with aura is part of the CADASIL phenotype, so attributing the transient hemiparesis to complicated migraine was not wrong about the phenomenon — it was wrong about the disease behind it
The genetic diagnosis changes the care of relatives as much as the patient's, which is why sequencing is required rather than optional once the phenotype is recognised
Triptans in a confirmed cerebral arteriopathy are a treatment to withdraw, and the migraine still needs prophylaxis by another route

red_herrings.data_point: Lifelong migraine with aura and two episodes labelled complicated migraine
red_herrings.intended_effect: Explains the transient neurological events and defers imaging and genetic testing for nine years
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Migraine with aura is a core feature of CADASIL rather than an alternative diagnosis, and the transient hemiparesis in this context was a subcortical infarct in a hereditary arteriopathy

red_herrings.data_point: Two previous depressive episodes that responded to treatment
red_herrings.intended_effect: Frames the current apathy and slowing as a third depressive episode
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The apathy is dissociated from mood on formal scales, is accompanied by a gait disorder, pyramidal signs and urinary urgency, and sits on a Fazekas 3 imaging burden — psychiatric presentations are themselves part of the CADASIL phenotype

key_educational_points: A severe small-vessel burden before 60 without vascular risk factors requires a hereditary explanation
Symmetric anterior temporal pole white matter involvement is the most specific imaging marker of CADASIL
Migraine with aura and psychiatric presentations are part of the CADASIL phenotype, not alternatives to it
A genetic diagnosis extends the duty of care to relatives through counselling
